voyage.name: Goa Gajah
voyage.price: Adults Rp 50.000, Kids Rp 25.000 including sarong
voyage.content: The centerpiece here is a cave dating back to the 9th century, the entrance to which is an ornately carved demon's mouth. Inside are some fragmentary lingam and yoni statues, as well as a statue of Ganesha. Large, carved guards stand around pools near the entrance, and a little path leads to a waterfall, rice fields, and some Buddhist stupa fragments. Some parts of the Goa Gajah complex were not excavated until the 1

voyage.name: Gunung Kawi
voyage.price: adult Rp30,000, child Rp 15,000 including sarong and sash rental
voyage.content: Dating from the eleventh century, this is presumed to be the burial complex of King Anak Wungsu and his many wives. Reached by climbing down 371 steps, the location at the bottom of a steep valley lined with paddy fields, is quite stunning. The smaller complex on the south side of the river is presumed to have been built for the King's wives, while the larger complex is thought to have been the residence of the King

voyage.name: Pura Kehen
voyage.content: One of the most attractive temples in the whole of Bali, and as it is slightly off the beaten path, one which receives relatively few visitors. The temple was founded in 1206, and has an especially impressive 11-tiered meru in the inner courtyard. When you visit here take a little extra time to look around Bangli. It is a quiet and attractive market town.

voyage.name: Puri Saren Agung
voyage.alt: Royal Palace, Water Palace, Ubud Palace
voyage.content: This was the palace of the kings of Ubud until the 1940s, and some royal descendants live there to this day. Parts of the complex are off limits to the public, but entry to the rest is free, and this is Ubud's best setting for dance performances (see Do). 10-15 min visit without a guide.

voyage.name: Tirta Empul
voyage.price: Rp50,000, including sarong and sash rental
voyage.content: One of the holiest temples in Bali built around hot springs that still bubble in the central courtyard. The Balinese come here to bathe and purify themselves physically and spiritually, and during Galungan, the sacred barong masks are bathed here. The complex dates to 960, but the present buildings are largely modern reconstructions. Visitors may participate in the traditional purification ritual (melukat) by wearing

voyage.name: Yeh Pulu
voyage.content: This complex of rock carvings is close to Goa Gajah but far less well known. The carvings date from the fourteenth or fifteenth century, and are set in a very attractive rice field. You can reach Yeh Pulu on foot through the rice fields from Goa Gajah, but you will definitely need a guide for the 45-minute walk as there is no path to speak of. In addition to the carvings, there is a holy well here, and the attendant

voyage.name: Chapel of Mother Goddess, Rajarajeshwari Tripurasundari
voyage.content: A modern chapel dedicated to the feminine aspect of the divine, such as Kuan Shih Yin, Mary Magdalene, Mother Mary, Lakshmi, Durga, Kali, Saraswati, Gayatri and others.

voyage.name: Saraswati Temple
voyage.content: Taman Saraswati Temple, also known as Pura Taman Kemuda Saraswati, is a graceful water temple located in the heart of Ubud, Bali. Dedicated to Saraswati, the Hindu goddess of wisdom, learning, and the arts, this temple is renowned not only for its spiritual significance but also for its striking beauty—especially the elegant lotus pond and water garden that stretch out in front of its ornately carved gates.^Built in

voyage.name: Pura Gunung Lebah
voyage.content: Pura Gunung Lebah sits at the confluence of the Campuhan and Wos rivers beside Campuhan Bridge. Dating from the 8th century, it is one of Ubud's oldest and most sacred temples. Dedicated to the spirit of the surrounding valleys, the temple is known for its peaceful atmosphere, traditional stone carvings and lush jungle setting. It also marks the southern entrance to the popular Campuhan Ridge Walk.

voyage.name: Agung Rai Museum of Art
voyage.content: Showcases works by well known Balinese artists, as well as international artists who made Bali their home such as Walter Spies, Adrian Jean Le Mayeur, Rudolph Bonnet and Arie Smit. The only painting in Bali by renowned Javanese artist Radan Saleh is exhibited here. They also run workshops for thirteen different aspects of Balinese art and culture. Price includes tea or coffee (hot or cold) at their cafe.

voyage.name: Blanco Renaissance Museum
voyage.content: Before he passed away in 1999, Spanish artist Antonio Blanco was an absolute fixture on the Ubud art scene. His former home is now a museum showcasing his sometimes bizarre but always interesting work. Think Salvador Dali transplanted to Asia. In the garden you can take pictures of the exotic birds flying around. A gallery and a studio is connected to the museum. Also, there is a family temple and a vegan restaurant

voyage.name: Museum Puri Lukisan
voyage.content: When it opened in 1954, this was the first private museum in Bali. Three buildings showcase traditional and modern Balinese art. The displays are a little musty and English labeling is spotty, but some of the works, particularly the carvings, are quite amazing. Exhibits by noted artists I Gusti Nyoman Lempad and Rudolph Bonnet, among others.

voyage.name: Museum Rudana
voyage.price: Rp20,000, under 12 years old is free
voyage.content: A wide range of Balinese paintings is exhibited here, both traditional and modern. Run by its owner, artist Nyoman Rudana, who is often present.

voyage.name: Neka Art Museum
voyage.price: Rp150.000 (adults), Rp75.000 (students with ID), Rp75.000 (6-12 years old), free (under 6 years old)
voyage.content: This museum houses perhaps the most important art collection in the whole of Bali. Six pavilions house the various collections which include dedicated rooms for artists Arie Smit and I Gusti Nyoman Lempad. See beautiful depictions of Balinese life in times past as well as contemporary works, both by Balinese artists and by the foreign artists who settled here. Mainly paintings but also some sculptures and photography

voyage.name: Setia Darma House of Masks and Puppets
voyage.content: This fascinating museum displays more than a thousand masks and puppets from across Indonesia and around the world. Traditional Balinese, Javanese and international theatrical traditions are represented within a peaceful complex of traditional wooden houses surrounded by gardens.

voyage.name: Tegallalang
voyage.content: Northeast of Ubud, the land starts to become more undulating, and this is a good place to view Bali's classic rice terraces. This village is somewhat a tourist trap, but it is worth braving the hordes of trinket peddlers to view the stunning terraces. From the town center, take Jl Raya as far east as you can go, and then turn north and continue about nine km until you reach Tegallalang. Look for the picture postcard

voyage.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
voyage.content: Located south of Ubud, Tegenungan Waterfall is one of Bali's most accessible waterfalls. A short walk down steps leads to a powerful cascade surrounded by tropical forest. Early morning visits avoid the largest crowds.

voyage.name: Tibumana Waterfall
voyage.content: Set within a forested valley east of Ubud, Tibumana Waterfall is a graceful single-drop cascade flowing into a calm swimming pool. The easy walk through bamboo groves and tropical vegetation makes it one of the area's most relaxing waterfalls.

voyage.name: Kanto Lampo Waterfall
voyage.content: Unlike most waterfalls, Kanto Lampo flows over a series of stepped rock terraces, creating one of Bali's most photographed natural attractions. Be prepared to get wet if climbing onto the rocks.

voyage.name: Bali Bird Park
voyage.address: Jl Serma Cok Ngurah Gambir, Singapadu
voyage.content: A splendid 2-hectare aviary park with more than 250 species of birds in well thought out, attractive enclosures. The park has an enlightened, modern attitude to exhibiting animals, and this is obvious from the very open, walk-in aviaries, and the number of free range birds throughout the park. Also has a notably good cafe. One of Bali's best formal attractions.

voyage.name: Botanic Garden
voyage.content: The Botanic Garden is a wonderful way to spend a few hours walking around and exploring the valley that it fills. It is best to go in the morning and avoid the afternoon heat.

voyage.name: Monkey Forest
voyage.content: A sacred forest full of monkeys, which are not at all afraid of people and will happily climb all over you if you're not careful! They love to look in backpacks and often take people's sunglasses or wallets. Don't bring any food or you will risk getting bitten. If you are bitten, visit the first aid clinic near the entrance at the bottom of Jalan Monkey Forest. You will need rabies shots. Stroll through to find Pura

voyage.name: The White Herons of Petulu
voyage.content: Every evening between 15,000 and 20,000 cattle egrets, known colloquially as white herons and in Balinese, kokokan, roost in the village of Petulu just ten minutes north of Ubud. It is quite a spectacle as these large, elegant white and rusty orange birds arrive in countless groups and tussle for the prime roosting spots. Each morning at dawn they leave en-masse to find feeding spots around the island. Some also bree

voyage.name: Penglipuran Village
voyage.content: One of Bali's best-preserved traditional villages, Penglipuran is renowned for its immaculate bamboo-lined streets, beautifully maintained family compounds and traditional Balinese architecture. Vehicles are kept outside the village, creating a peaceful atmosphere that offers a glimpse into traditional Balinese community life.

voyage.name: Pyramids of Chi
voyage.content: Pyramids of Chi is a wellness centre offering sound healing, meditation and relaxation sessions inside pyramid-shaped buildings designed to enhance acoustics. Sessions combine music, vibration and guided meditation.

voyage.name: Blanco Gardens
voyage.content: The gardens surrounding the Blanco Renaissance Museum feature tropical landscaping, sculptures and free-roaming exotic birds. They provide a peaceful setting overlooking the Campuhan valley.

voyage.name: Bali Swing
voyage.content: Bali Swing offers giant swings suspended high above jungle valleys and rice terraces, along with a variety of photo platforms. While primarily designed for photography, it has become one of Bali's best-known attractions.

voyage.name: Nyuh Kuning Village
voyage.content: Just south of the Monkey Forest, Nyuh Kuning is a quiet village of cafés, gardens and traditional homes. Wide tree-lined streets make it a pleasant place for a leisurely walk away from central Ubud.

voyage.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk
voyage.content: Campuhan Ridge Walk begins beside the Pura Gunung Lebah and follows a gently undulating 2 km paved ridge trail. This walk was recommended in the early 21st century but as of 2026 the views have sadly been ruined by development. Still, it is a nice enough walk. The best way to do it is to take a Grab to Bankiang Sidem, the village on the northern end of the walk. This way, you'll be walking downhill 2km back into cent

voyage.name: Sari Organik Walk
voyage.content: The Sari Organik Walk is an easy stroll through rice fields immediately north of central Ubud. Passing small cafés, traditional farms and coconut palms, it offers a peaceful escape from the busy streets and is especially pleasant early in the morning or around sunset.

voyage.name: Kajeng Rice Field Walk
voyage.content: This pleasant walk begins near Jalan Kajeng and quickly leaves central Ubud behind, passing rice fields, small cafés and traditional homes. It is quieter than the Campuhan Ridge Walk and offers a glimpse of everyday village life.

voyage.name: Sweet Orange Walk
voyage.content: The Sweet Orange Walk is even better than the Campuhan Ridge Walk was before it was ruined by development. It follows narrow paths through rice fields just north of central Ubud, passing cafés, rice fields, homestays and art studios. It is a relaxing walk suitable for most visitors. Loop back into central Ubud by turning onto Jalan Kajeng and browse its art and trinket stalls.

voyage.name: Bali Center for Artistic Creativity (BCAC)
voyage.content: Art studio nestled in beautiful grounds and galleries offering art classes from beginners to teachers, and internationally accredited courses run by Bruce Sherratt.

voyage.name: Payuk Bali Home Cooking Class
voyage.content: Traditional Balinese cooking such as sate lilit, Balinese salad, and nasi kuning.

voyage.name: Paon Bali Cooking Class
voyage.content: Traditional Balinese cooking class in the home of a very hospitable family. They offer a pick-up in Ubud.

voyage.name: Pemulan Bali - Balinese Farm Cooking School
voyage.alt: first farm cooking school in Ubud
voyage.content: A new community project to save the organic farmer in the village. They have the cooking classes every day for vegetarians and meat lovers. The program consists of a visit to a local market, an organic farm tour, picking some ingredients for cooking and hands-on cooking experience (you will cook your food).

voyage.name: Ubad Ubud Bali Cooking Class
voyage.address: Jln. Ki Pasung Grigis, Banjar Tengkulak Kaja, Desa Kemenuh
voyage.content: Introduction to the exotic ingredients and unique culinary heritage of Bali, set in Balinese compound.

voyage.name: Ubud Cooking Class with Putu
voyage.price: Cooking class and meal: US$60 for one adult; US$45 per person for 2–4 adults; US$40 per person for 5 or more adults. The market-tour option costs more.
voyage.address: Banjar Pesalakan, Pejeng Kangin, Gianyar, Bali
voyage.content: Private Balinese cooking class at Putu's family compound in Pejeng, near Ubud. Guests prepare five dishes and eat the meal they make. A morning market visit is available with a separate package. Pickup and return from accommodation in Ubud are included.

voyage.name: Barong Dance
voyage.content: Kecak and fire dance at 6:30 and Barong dance at 09:30, every day. Each lasts about an hour and the ticket is sold separately. Barong dance is very much a performance for tourists, and the story is of the never-ending battle between good and evil. There is actually not much dancing and a lot of talking in this performance. While buying a ticket, you will get an outdated description of the forthcoming performance.

voyage.name: Pura Dalem
voyage.content: One of the best kecak performances in Ubud, every Friday and Monday evening. Staged in beautiful surroundings outside under the banyan trees, and followed by a fire dance. Excellent ambiance and the fire dance at the end is impressive. A leaflet in several languages is at disposal to understand the illustrated Ramayana story. However, parts of the performance can get repetitive.

voyage.name: Puri Saren & Puri Saraswati
voyage.alt: just east of Jl Monkey Forest
voyage.content: Smack dab in the centre of town, dance performances are staged here almost nightly.

voyage.name: Bali Healing
voyage.content: Even for the experienced massage consumer, this six-bed massage centre is an experience. A 1-hr massage is about Rp80,000. Magic warm stone massage for Rp120,000. Several other deep tissue and reflexology treatments are available

voyage.name: Bamboo Bali Spa
voyage.content: Friendly and attentive service in a comfortable setting, with interiors featuring soft cream colours and tasteful ornaments. The therapists deliver top-notch therapeutic massages. You can enjoy cups of comforting rosella or ginger tea at the cosy seating area after treatment.

voyage.name: Sang Spa
voyage.content: Small full-service day spa, owned and run by a young couple named Ngurah and Asti. Simple, secluded, clean and nicely decorated. Very professional staff.

voyage.name: SenS Spa
voyage.address: 1 Jalan Sukma, junction of Jalan Raya Ubud and Jalan Sukma
voyage.content: SenS Spa, inside the SenS Hotel & Spa, features 1 couples treatment suite, 2 single suites and 3 foot reflexology stations.

voyage.name: Ubud Sari Health Resort
voyage.content: Emphasis on Balinese-style healing therapy. Offers alternative health care, a day spa, beauty salon, health massage, vegetarian restaurant and yoga.

voyage.name: Verona Spa
voyage.content: Private individual or coupled rooms that open onto a rice terrace. 4-hour package called the Verona Spa Experience has a massage, body scrub, flower bath, facial, manicure, pedicure, and hair creme bath (not to be missed if you like having your head massaged).

voyage.name: Tamarind Spa
voyage.content: Excellent spa with professional and well qualified therapists. which attracts rave reviews. Full spa menu and spa packages menu. They are also able to give massage training lessons. www.murnis.com.

voyage.name: Pertenin Body Care
voyage.content: Facial treatments and massage in a relaxing, modern environment. Customer may select the oils and herbs for any treatment.

voyage.name: Adventure & Spirit
voyage.content: Canyoning is an outdoor adventure and sport using a variety of techniques that may include walking, abseiling, jumping, sliding down natural slopes and swimming in white water for aquatic canyons. And of course discover beautiful and hidden places at the heart of Balinese nature.

voyage.name: Bali Countryside Cycling
voyage.content: A/C hotel return, 3½ hours downhill biking, Light Breakfast, Bike and Safety equipment, Guide, Mineral water en route, Lunch and Insurance covered.

voyage.name: Bali Bintang Tour
voyage.content: Hotel transfer, light breakfast overlooking Mt. Batur, well maintained bikes, water en route, lunch, insurance covered.

voyage.name: Bali Budaya Eco Tours
voyage.content: Free pickup from hotel, breakfast with a view of Mount Batur, visit to coffee plantation, downhill cycling through rice paddies and villages, visit to a Balinese family compound, optional flat/uphill cycling and a generous buffet lunch. Two guides per group, bikes in good condition, helmets, water also included. Also do volcano climbs, jungle treks, etc.

voyage.name: Bali Bike Adventures
voyage.content: Includes return hotel transfer, mountain bike with safety helmet, breakfast, towel and mineral water, all entrance fees, professional guide, buffet lunch, insurance covered for each participant.

voyage.name: Bali Hai Adventures Specialist
voyage.content: See the Bali countryside at a leisurely pace on a bicycle. Includes private A/C van (min 2 pax booking), mountain bike and safety helmet, breakfast and lunch, fruit and mineral water on tour, entrance fees and personal insurance coverage.

voyage.name: Bali Adventure Tours
voyage.content: Established in 1989, one of the first whitewater rafting adventures in Bali. They offer packages that include their elephant safari park & lodge, cycling, rafting and an elephant safari. Free pickup from hotel. US$100,000 insurance is provided.

voyage.name: Sobek Bali Utama
voyage.content: Specialise in white-water rafting and cycling tours. Established in 1989, this was the first company of its type in Bali, and they are distinctly less package-oriented than their main competitor.

voyage.name: Ubud Yoga Centre
voyage.price: From Rp160,000 per session. Ten class pass for Rp1,200,000, monthly unlimited for Rp2,250,000
voyage.address: Singakerta Raya No. 108 (Jembatan Nyuh Kuning), Nyuh Kuning, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali 80571
voyage.content: Expat-run centre offers everything from single attendance classes up to residential yoga instructor training courses.

voyage.name: The Yoga Barn
voyage.content: The most well known and the biggest studio in Ubud. Offers a huge of classes (can get up to 30+ different classes every day) and an excellent set of teachers mostly in the Ashtanga/Vinnyasa school. At the same time - can be quite crowded without much of the individual approach because of the scale. Upper studio has great views of the surrounding rice terraces. Residential packages, multiple day classes and simple sin

voyage.name: Alchemy Yoga and Meditation Center
voyage.content: One of the several major yoga centers in Ubud, offering quite a unique classes which are usually called like "Fire / Ether / Earth Class" with different goals and practices in a beautiful setting. Has a restaurant with the same name nearby.

voyage.name: Radiantly Alive Yoga
voyage.price: Starting from a 165'000 for a single drop-in class
voyage.content: Pleasant and well-known studio in the center of Ubud offering a variety of classes

voyage.name: Intuitive Flow
voyage.address: Banjar Penestanan Kaja, Jl. Raya Campuan Jalan, Sayan, Kecamatan Ubud
voyage.content: One of the most well known yoga studios with good reviews to the west from the center

voyage.name: Anand Ashram@Ubud
voyage.content: Non-profit institution offering yoga, meditation, satsang, kirtan, bed and breakfast. Visiting teachers and students are welcome to use the space for their programs and stay on donation basis.

voyage.name: Bali Yoga School
voyage.content: Offers yoga classes with a creative blend of the classical and modern yoga philosophies. Their courses in Bikram, Iyengar, Ashtanga, Dharma, and Forest Yoga are challenging but can heal physical and mental problems with fun.

voyage.name: Firefly Yoga Retreat
voyage.content: Retreats start from 350 EUR per person.

voyage.name: Taman Hati Yoga and Meditation Center
voyage.content: This centre was founded in 2000 by two local men, both from families containing many generations of Hindu priests. Set up for both complete beginners, and those already experienced but wishing to broaden their horizons. Every Wednesday at 19:30, there is a free class entitled "World Peace Meditation".

voyage.name: Bali Yoga Teacher Training Center
voyage.content: Yoga school with instructors from diverse regions, bringing a variety of yoga styles.

voyage.name: Bali Yoga Teacher Training Center (Bali YTTC)
voyage.address: Villas Dur Pekerisan, Bitera, Gianyar Regency, Ubud
voyage.content: Yoga Alliance certified RYS 200/300 yoga school located in a peaceful jungle river valley in Bitera, 10-15 minutes outside central Ubud. Offers 21-day residential Hatha, Ashtanga & Vinyasa teacher training courses with organic plant-based meals and villa accommodations.

voyage.name: Ubud Market
voyage.content: This is a double storey warren of stalls bursting at the seams with wood carvings, batik shirts, sarongs, and all manner of other souvenirs aimed specifically at tourists. The merchants here haggle with tourists for a living, and think nothing of asking for ten times the going price, so try to establish a baseline before you go in to buy. Most of the merchants downstairs will lose interest if you try to get a reasona

voyage.name: Ganesha Bookstore
voyage.content: Second hand bookstore. Also has great range of new books about Bali and Indonesia. Been around since 1986 and now has a second branch in Seminyak.

voyage.name: Pondok Pekak Library & Learning Centre
voyage.content: This privately run community library often has decent fiction and other books for sale. By buying here you are supporting their mission to make free books available to Balinese schoolkids. When you visit, check to see if they have any cultural performances coming up. Also has a small cafe serving home-made snacks.

voyage.name: Sukawati Art Market
voyage.content: This huge market is like a one-stop centre for all the craft villages between Sanur and Ubud. Many souvenir shop owners from around Bali wholesale purchase their items here, and prices are considerably lower than in the tourist centers like Kuta, Sanur, and Ubud town centre. For a taste of everyday, go to the food and produce market opposite the art market.

voyage.name: Threads of Life
voyage.content: A fair trade store that stocks commercially made, traditional hand-woven textiles from Bali and all points east in Indonesia. Or better yet, go to the shops that are actually from the villages and outer islands like Timor and Flores, and specialize in traditional weavings.

voyage.name: Bubu Warung
voyage.content: Healthy and delicious Balinese cuisine with plenty of choices on the menu. If you have any special requests, Ibu Made will be happy to cater for you.

voyage.name: Dewa Warung
voyage.content: Dewa's is one of the better cheap places to eat in town. Serves all the usual Balinese and Indonesian dishes. Most mains Rp24,000 - 36,000.

voyage.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka 1
voyage.content: A Bali culinary experience. The babi guling (spit-roasted pig) here is world-famous, and this humble eating place is virtually a place of pilgrimage. The roast pork is served with rice and spiced veggies, order the special (Rp55,000) to get a bit of everything — including offal and blood sausage. There are normal tables and chairs but you can also sit on the floor at low tables inside the bale (pavilion).

voyage.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka 2
voyage.content: Unlike the original, where comfort and appearance are not strong points, this outlet is a two-storey restaurant which is spotless, airy and comfortable.

voyage.name: Pizza Bagus
voyage.content: Provides fresh made to order pizzas, pasta and other Italian style meals. Italian gelato and a full deli are also available. Eat-in, take-out or delivery. Organic market held every Saturday morning. Games and TV are provided to entertain children. Free wifi.

voyage.name: Sawah Indah Resto Ubud
voyage.content: Lunch or dinner with a rice field view. Fish pond. Relaxing and good for a family or group.

voyage.name: Sari Bamboo
voyage.content: A tourist class warung, with food freshly cooked to order, set amid tropical gardens on the main road to Penestanan village. Mainly Indonesian food flavoured to suit the taste of western visitors. The warung and bungalows are easily distinguishable by the display of modern art works by the resident artist. No hard sell though, just good food in beautiful surroundings at good prices. Serves breakfast, lunch and dinner

voyage.name: Warung biah biah
voyage.content: Mainly rice and noodle-based dishes.

voyage.name: Warung Nasi Ayam Kedewatan Ibu Mangku
voyage.content: authentic Balinese mixed rice.

voyage.name: Sun Sun Warung
voyage.content: One of Ubud's best-loved local warungs, Sun Sun Warung serves authentic Balinese cooking in a relaxed atmosphere. Housed in a rustic double-storey building with gardens and pavillions to sit in as well. Excellent food and service.

voyage.name: Warung Siam
voyage.content: Warung Siam brings authentic Thai flavours to central Ubud with fragrant curries, spicy salads, noodle dishes and traditional stir-fries. Fresh ingredients, generous portions and reasonable prices make it one of the town's most reliable choices for Thai food.

voyage.name: Warung Mangga Madu
voyage.content: Popular with locals and travellers looking for authentic flavours, Warung Mangga Madu specialises in freshly prepared Balinese and Indonesian favourites. Its relaxed atmosphere and consistently good food make it one of Ubud's hidden culinary gems.

voyage.name: Warung Lokal
voyage.content: Warung Lokal offers excellent Indonesian comfort food in a clean, modern setting. The varied menu includes everything from nasi goreng and satay to regional specialties, making it a reliable choice for an inexpensive meal.

voyage.name: Sayuri Healing Food
voyage.content: Sayuri Healing Food has become one of Ubud's best-known vegan restaurants. The menu features colourful organic dishes, raw food creations, smoothies and fresh juices, with an emphasis on healthy, nutrient-rich ingredients and sustainable eating.

voyage.name: Fu Shou Noodle Club
voyage.content: Fu Shou Noodle Club focuses on freshly made noodles inspired by regional Chinese cuisine. Handmade dumplings, rich broths and bold flavours have quickly earned it a reputation as one of Ubud's best noodle restaurants.

voyage.name: Alchemy
voyage.content: A 100% raw vegan organic cafe & juice bar, organic health food store, and holistic clinic. Yummy breakfast bar with fruits, nuts, seeds, and raw vegan organic nutmilks and yoghurts from 07:00-11:00, delicious salad bar with amazing superfoods and toppings from 11:00-21:00. Alchemy has an Instagram account at @alchemybali.

voyage.name: Kafe Batan Waru
voyage.content: Long established Ubud institution. Excellent Balinese and other Indonesian food as well as western options, in a well designed space. Also serves top quality coffee, and has a dessert menu which includes an especially notable version of Balinese black rice pudding (bubur injin). Indoor and outdoor seating.

voyage.name: Clear Cafe
voyage.content: An organic cafe with a variety of vegetarian, vegan, and raw food-friendly selections. Free Wi-Fi. Try free samples from their bakery at the front of the restaurant!

voyage.name: Cafe des Artistes
voyage.content: This Belgian-owned eatery serves Indonesian dishes as well as a vast array of international classics. Famous for their grilled tenderloin steaks. Extensive winelist, cocktails, Belgian beers and homemade desserts. Free wifi from 11:00-18:00. To make sure you get a table for dinner, call ahead.

voyage.name: Casa Luna
voyage.content: Large, long-established restaurant serving western and local dishes, and plenty that fall somewhere in between.

voyage.name: Murni's Warung
voyage.content: Excellent western and Balinese food in a stunning, gorge setting. Elegant lounge bar. Historic, being the 1st real restaurant in Ubud founded by Murni herself in 1974. Also a shop with interesting collectibles and the odd real antique.

voyage.name: Naughty Nuri's Warung and Grill
voyage.content: Crowded roadside watering hole. Microbrews, great martinis and slabs of BBQ ribs. This is very much a standard stop for Korean or Japanese tour buses. Once a week they do amazing grilled tuna. Careful that the waitresses do not stick other peoples drinks on your bill. A few times a year they have parties where drinks are US$10 for as much beer as you can handle, for example during USA elections and the Superbowl.

voyage.name: Nomad
voyage.content: A long-standing institution that serves up a good selection of Balinese, Indonesian, and western dishes, but deservedly popular is their version of a tapas selection, consisting of bite-sized portions of local flavors. 12 pieces of tapas served with rice costs Rp90,000 and feeds two. Also serves a wide range of cocktails and spirits.

voyage.name: Taco Casa
voyage.content: Mexican Restaurant. Open kitchen, simple and fresh tacos (soft and crispy), nachos, 8-layer burrito, fajitas, cheesy enchiladas, quesadillas and taco salad bowl. Fresh blended tropical fruit juices or lassies, milkshakes, freshly prepared lemonade, pure juices, mineral water, hot drink, margarita, mojito, sangria and soft drinks.

voyage.name: Uma Resto
voyage.content: Provides an Asian (Balinese, Indonesian, Thai) and Western cuisine, and various of beverages; cocktail, mocktail, coffee or tea. Free wifi

voyage.name: Wild Vegan
voyage.content: Vegan restaurant.

voyage.name: Milk & Madu Ubud
voyage.content: Outstanding breakfasts and artisan coffee, wood-fired pizzas and hearty lunches. The beautiful high-ceilinged light-filled room gets quite warm on hot days.

voyage.name: Hujan Locale
voyage.content: Created by renowned chef Will Meyrick, Hujan Locale celebrates Indonesia's extraordinary regional cuisine through beautifully presented modern dishes. Combining traditional recipes with contemporary techniques, it has become one of Ubud's leading destinations for Indonesian fine casual dining.

voyage.name: Nusantara by Locavore
voyage.content: Nusantara by Locavore showcases the incredible diversity of Indonesian cuisine, with recipes collected from islands across the archipelago. Beautifully prepared and presented, it offers one of the best opportunities in Bali to explore authentic regional cooking beyond the familiar Balinese classics.

voyage.name: Donna
voyage.content: Donna combines Mediterranean flavours with a lively rooftop atmosphere, offering tapas, grilled meats, seafood, handcrafted cocktails and live music. Its stylish setting makes it one of Ubud's most popular evening dining destinations.

voyage.name: Zest
voyage.content: Set beside the Campuhan valley, Zest has earned a reputation as one of Bali's finest vegan restaurants. The creative menu features beautifully presented plant-based dishes inspired by Indonesian and international flavours, complemented by excellent coffee, juices and desserts.

voyage.name: The Elephant
voyage.content: The Elephant combines fresh vegetarian cuisine with one of Ubud's most peaceful dining locations overlooking the Campuhan valley. Seasonal ingredients, excellent coffee and panoramic views make it a favourite for breakfast, brunch or a relaxed lunch.

voyage.name: Seed Eatery
voyage.content: Seed Eatery offers quality coffee, fresh breakfasts and creative brunch dishes prepared with seasonal ingredients. Bright interiors, friendly service and consistently excellent food have quickly made it one of Ubud's favourite cafés.

voyage.name: Umah Pizza
voyage.content: Uma Pizza specialises in authentic wood-fired pizzas made with quality ingredients and traditional techniques. Fresh pasta, salads and Italian desserts complete a menu that has made it one of Ubud's favourite casual Italian restaurants.

voyage.name: Honey & Smoke
voyage.content: Honey & Smoke celebrates cooking over fire with expertly grilled meats, seafood and seasonal vegetables. Mediterranean influences, creative cocktails and stylish surroundings make it an excellent choice for an evening meal.

voyage.name: Mazzoni Pizza
voyage.content: Mazzoni Pizza brings traditional Italian flavours to Ubud with slow-fermented dough, wood-fired pizzas and homemade pasta. Friendly service and consistently high-quality ingredients have made it a favourite among both visitors and local residents.

voyage.name: Pukako
voyage.content: Nestled in the rice fields of North Ubud, this cafe-restaurant has beautiful views from its lovely outdoor eating area. Fantastic paninis, smoothie bowls, and western delights

voyage.name: Bebek Bengil
voyage.content: An interesting restaurant with paddy field views and nice gardens. Famous for their crispy fried duck and some European-based menu items. They have a good selection of cakes as well. Free wifi in the area closest to the street.

voyage.name: Cascades Restaurant
voyage.content: A fine dining restaurant with French inspired menus mixed with Asian influences. Good views and hushed atmosphere. Has a large wine list.

voyage.name: Mozaic
voyage.content: The brainchild of chef Chris Salans, this is one of the leading restaurants in the whole of Bali, and one which will please even the most jaded of foodies. Multi-award winning, including the coveted Les Grandes Tables du Monde award (the only restaurant in Bali ever to achieve that). Western prices, but worth it as a special treat. Try the degustation menu.

voyage.name: Apéritif Restaurant
voyage.content: Views of a jungle valley and colonial-era decor, under the guidance of chef Nic Vanderbeeken.

voyage.name: Locavore NXT
voyage.content: Locavore NXT continues the legacy of one of Asia's most celebrated restaurants. Combining cutting-edge culinary techniques with locally sourced ingredients and a strong focus on sustainability, it offers an unforgettable tasting-menu experience that ranks among Indonesia's finest dining destinations.

voyage.name: Room4Dessert
voyage.content: Created by award-winning chef Will Goldfarb, Room4Dessert is unlike any other restaurant in Bali. Multi-course dessert tasting menus are paired with creative savoury bites and cocktails, making it one of Ubud's most original and internationally recognised dining experiences.

voyage.name: Sayan House
voyage.content: Perched above the Ayung River gorge, Sayan House combines Japanese precision with bold Latin American flavours. Creative cocktails, beautifully presented dishes and breathtaking sunset views have made it one of Ubud's premier dinner venues.

voyage.name: The Melting Pot Game Room and Pub
voyage.content: Pool hall and games room with full bar. Every nation is represented with a flag and customers are encouraged to sign their country’s flag. Food, music, table tennis, darts, foosball, video games, pool tables, and a general atmosphere make it a place where locals, ex-pats, and tourists often congregate. 8 Ball tournaments every Tuesday night and 10 ball tournaments on Fridays are open to all.

voyage.name: Bali Pulina
voyage.address: Jl. Raya Pujung Kaja, Sebatu, Tegallalang
voyage.content: Sprawling venue with lush, tropical vegetation, coffee and tea tastings, also a zipline through the foliage. Try Kopi Luwak.

voyage.name: Seniman Coffee Studio
voyage.address: Jl. Sri Wedari No.5, Banjar Taman Kelod
voyage.content: A popular retro cafe that serves a variety of selected coffees & food from several local regions.

voyage.name: Fold
voyage.content: This cafe-bakery-pizza place-restaurant has the best barista coffee in Ubud. They also have the excellent, local Kura Kura beer on tap.

voyage.name: Dewi Antara Homestay
voyage.content: A humble Balinese family homestay. Quiet and clean bungalows in a garden setting. The father participates in cultural activities (he's a dancer), so it's fun to watch him in traditional dress. Mum prepares the breakfast of toast, fruit salad and coffee.

voyage.name: Family Guest House
voyage.content: Friendly Hindu family makes you feel right at home. Rooms are placed in a lovely compound and includes a good breakfast.

voyage.name: Gustis Garden Bungalows
voyage.content: Balinese style with 25 m sq, private balcony, private bathroom. hot and cold water, king size bed, clothing cabinet, dressing table, ceiling fan, wash basin and standing shower.

voyage.name: Jati Home Stay
voyage.content: Rooms using natural, traditional materials of bamboo, marble and thatched roofs. An atmosphere of art and culture, all members of Jati's family are traditional Balinese artists. Learn Balinese painting and watch a group of children practice Balinese dancing.

voyage.name: Bali Traditional Homestay
voyage.address: Jl Raya Bono, Bona Kelod, Blahbatuh, Gianyar
voyage.content: Rooms with private bathroom with cold and hot shower, overlooking rice fields. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Melati Cottages
voyage.content: Traditional style rooms set around a cafe by a pool. You can walk in from north or south.

voyage.name: Narasoma Homestay
voyage.address: Gang Beji off Jl Monkey Forest
voyage.content: Down a little lane off busy Jl Monkey Forest. Family home with accommodation. Balinese compound setting with traditional carved buildings, surrounded by coconut palms. Top floor has views of the central mountains and Mount Agung. Clean and airy, and breakfast is included.

voyage.name: Nyoman Murjana Homestay
voyage.price: Double with hot shower from Rp200,000
voyage.content: Clean, nicely furnished rooms in a traditional Balinese family compound. A breakfast is included with egg, toast, veggies, fresh fruit, coffee and tea, also has WiFi. The family can help with information, bicycle and motorbike rental.

voyage.name: Rumah Roda Homestay and Restaurant
voyage.content: Lovely family compound with rooms. The restaurant has a Sunday evening buffet. The book A Little Bit One O'Clock is about this place and family.

voyage.name: Shana Homestay
voyage.content: 3 bungalows in garden setting, each with 2 beds, breakfast included.

voyage.name: Raka's House
voyage.content: Quiet family homestay, bungalows with and without AC, free wifi, small pool.

voyage.name: The Onion Collective
voyage.price: Rooms Rp 472,500, studio cabins Rp 585,000 incl. breakfast
voyage.content: Several unique cozy rooms, dorms, and a co-working space. Several comfortable places to hang out, inside and outside. Very friendly host and staff. Small menu but very tasty (burgers, dragon bowl, salads). Close to Yoga Barn, Hubud, Monkey Forest.

voyage.name: Ayuk Guest House
voyage.content: Sweet Balinese family run guest house, with three spacious double rooms; fans, Wi-Fi, full breakfast (pancakes or omelettes plus fruit and coffee/tea) cooked by Ayu. Nyoman, the husband, is also a driver, and they'll go out of their way to assist you with transport or needs. Rates are US$20 for one person, $30 for two.

voyage.name: Sunarta House Homestay
voyage.content: Nice and comfortable, Apr 2018 - Rp200,000 double room no hot water bathroom inside, nice breakfast - Rp250,000 for double fan room with hot water (not always work) bathroom inside, nice breakfast include.

voyage.name: Cucu House
voyage.content: A complex of bungalows surrounded by beautiful foliage, with both comfort and fresh air. Feels like you're out in the country with roosters crowing. Popular with couples. Check-in is hard to find, but just enter the complex and ask for directions (say "Cucu House", pronounced like "choo-choo") and someone will help you. Free, delicious breakfast served on the porch outside your room. Wifi is available but slow.

voyage.name: Aru house Ubud
voyage.content: dorm 10-beds, wifi, aircon, bedlight, power x1, curtains, locker (need padlock), attached one toilet (toilet paper, toilet gun)+one shower, no towel, no soap. small common area with water refill, tea, coffee, small fridge. Activities via Jalan-Jalan Wisata Rp 200,00-350,000/person.

voyage.name: Nua house
voyage.content: dorm 6-beds, wifi, aircon, bedlight, power x1, curtains, locker (need padlock), attached one toilet (toilet paper, toilet gun)+one shower, extra separated toilet+shower, optional towel (Rp 10,000), soap. small balcony, common area with water refill, tea, coffee.

voyage.name: Anom Cottages
voyage.content: Small bungalows with lovely views over the adjacent valley. 3 min from the town centre.

voyage.name: Bucu View Resort
voyage.content: 8 bedrooms, all tastefully furnished.

voyage.name: Dewa Bungalows
voyage.content: Family compound close to the center of town. Family-run and gracious, it has nice little slate pool perfect for a dip in the heat of the day. There is free access to WiFi as well as a restaurant.

voyage.name: Dewa Bharata Bungalows
voyage.content: Balinese-style accommodation, double bed, twin bed, public pool, direct IDD phone, TV, free Wi-Fi, airport transport, motorbike rental, breakfast, restaurant.

voyage.name: De Munut Resort
voyage.content: Traditional Balinese architecture with spa, public swimming pool, internet services, free Wi-Fi, deluxe room, super deluxe room.

voyage.name: Bali T House Klod
voyage.content: 1, 2 and 3 bedroom private villas in a traditional rice farming and carving area 5 km from central Ubud. Daily maid and breakfast service included. Shared pool with rice-field views. This is an environmentally friendly and ecologically sustainable compound and part of a Balinese village.

voyage.name: Jiwa Damai Bali Retreat
voyage.content: Organic (permaculture) garden and retreat centre in small village close to Ubud. 6 modern minimalist styled rooms with king size, queen size or two twin bed and three garden lumbungs. Spacious open air lounge and dining area, fresh water pool, organic fruit and vegetables used to prepare meals. Yoga and meditation classes for guests. Facilities available for seminars and retreats.

voyage.name: Munari Resort and Spa Ubud
voyage.content: 5-10 min by car to Ubud center, Free Wifi in room, option of twin and double bed, room full AC, swimming pool, free bicycle to use based on request, Bakmie MG Restaurant specialty in noodles. All rooms with balcony overlooking nice garden, swimming pool. 2nd floor room can enjoy the beauty of ricefield next to Munari.

voyage.name: Oka Kartini Bungalow
voyage.content: Quirky old Balinese house complex on the edge of town. The rooms here are a bit long in the tooth, but decorated with more carvings and gold paint than the average temple. Friendly staff supervised by the owner Oka Kartini. Large art gallery, a small but pleasant garden pool. Shadow puppet shows 3 days a week (extra charge).

voyage.name: Puri Asri Villa & Spa
voyage.content: In a very quiet spot south of town. Offer a couple of scheduled shuttle rides to Jl Monkey Forest and back each day. Walking distance from town via the Monkey Forest. Villas have spacious rooms, A/C, bath and shower (including outdoor showers), patio. Breakfast delivered to room if you choose. Take cash as their credit card facilities don't always work.

voyage.name: Puri Padi Hotel
voyage.content: A Balinese style hotel in green gardens. A tad rundown but with lovely staff.

voyage.name: Puri Saraswati Bungalows
voyage.content: Puri Saraswati is located in the centre of Ubud Village. Rooms are set back from the road and quiet and there's a pool and WiFi. Airport transfers are available.

voyage.name: Sania's house
voyage.content: Beautiful place with clean rooms, swimming pool. Wi-Fi and breakfast included.

voyage.name: Sri Aksata Ubud Resort
voyage.content: 16 bungalow-style rooms in lush gardens. 50 m from the busy road, but very quiet except for the singing of birds. Simple but pleasant rooms with bamboo furniture, western toilets and hot water. Large pool with rice paddies beyond. Internet cafe on the premises.

voyage.name: Sri Ratih Cottages
voyage.content: 30 rooms. Large peaceful garden, good-sized pool, free wifi for guests, 24 hr room service. Long staying guests may find good value here.

voyage.name: Suastika Bed and Breakfast
voyage.price: Rp250,000-400,000, breakfast and tax included, price negotiable if you stay for one week
voyage.content: Suastika is a Hindu symbol of peace. The rooms overlook family temples and beautiful jungle gardens, they all include a kitchen, large bathtub, shower and large huge bed. Breakfast is included with Bali coffee, pancakes, fruit all served on your private porch.

voyage.name: Taman Indrakila
voyage.content: Boutique hotel high above the Campuhan River Valley in Sangginan. All rooms have a private terrace.

voyage.name: Ubud Terrace Bungalows
voyage.content: Refurbished in 2008. Breakfast included, swimming pool, friendly staff. Tour and shuttle buses booking service.

voyage.name: Uma Sari Cottages
voyage.content: Balinese style thatch, wood and bamboo cottages surrounded by rice fields.

voyage.name: Hibiscus Cottages
voyage.content: Family-run, includes breakfast served on your patio. 7 Balinese style concrete cottages surrounded by rice fields. 2 A/C rooms are more expensive but built in 2010. Views from the 2nd storey cottages. Booking by phone is recommended.

voyage.name: Villa Indah
voyage.content: Breakfast included. Friendly Balinese family. 2 rooms and one suite, all have terrace and bathroom with hot water and tub. Stone villa in the middle of the rice fields. Self service kitchen. Motorbike for rent.

voyage.name: Villa JJ & Spa Ubud
voyage.price: From US$36 for One-Bedroom Joglo Villa, one kid up to 2 years old is free
voyage.content: 4-stars villa. Breakfast included. Pet-friendly accommodation. Has sun terrace and 3 outdoor swimming pools. Surrounding by paddy fields. Far from the crowd, Ubud Palace is more than 4 kilometers away and Ubud Monkey Forest is 6 kilometers away.

voyage.name: Pondok Pundi Village Inn
voyage.content: 11 guest rooms, each including mini bar, shower, bathrobes, refrigerator in central Ubud.

voyage.name: Taman Harum Cottages
voyage.content: Consists of 17 lovely rooms, restaurant, bar, swimming pool with a view of rice paddies, yoga/meditation room. Offers aerobic class, woodcarving studio & workshops.

voyage.name: Murni's Houses and Tamarind Spa
voyage.content: Very comfortable, quiet accommodation, excellent spa and meals can be delivered from Murni's Warung restaurant. Breakfast included. Architecturally impressive. All rooms have verandahs and are fly-screened. Pick ups and drops at the airport or anywhere else can be arranged. Tours, classes and activities can also be arranged. Free Wifi. www.murnis.com. From about US$60.

voyage.name: Bali Dream Resort & Spa
voyage.content: cozy accommodations with an outdoor swimming pool, an on-site restaurant and free Wi-Fi access in all areas of the property. Located in Penestanan Ubud area, a five minute drive from Ubud Centre and a five minute walk from the Antonio Blanco Museum.

voyage.name: Ayu Duwur Beji
voyage.content: Large and clean bungalow with a beautiful semi outdoor bathroom,nice view in to the jungle valley, great infinity pool and a very kind owner.

voyage.name: Alam Dania Cottage
voyage.content: Pool and the gardens are stunning and surrounded by breathtaking jungle, Cottage is small but cosy and comfy.

voyage.name: Bale Bali Inn
voyage.content: Rooms at Bale Bali Inn provide a flat screen TV, air conditioning, and a minibar, and guests can stay connected with free wifi.

voyage.name: Desak Putu Putera Cottages
voyage.content: within walking distance of city center and monkey forest area. The rooms were clean and safe. Breakfast was pretty good.

voyage.name: The Pari Sudha
voyage.content: Nice place with forest view, but access area have to walk.

voyage.name: Taman Rahasia
voyage.content: 8-room boutique hotel with a lush tropical garden in quiet part of Penestanan. Spa, restaurant and good-sized pool. Free WiFi & free shuttle bus service to Ubud town centre. Does not accept families with children under 7 yr.

voyage.name: Amandari
voyage.content: This was the first Aman hotel in Bali. It is getting a little bit tired but is still most impressive. Good views, tennis court, spa, restaurant. A luxury resort with no TVs.

voyage.name: Amori Villa
voyage.content: A boutique retreat 3 km from Ubud overlooking Petanu River Valley. Opened in June 2009. Butler service, good food and wine. 5 private suites/villas, all with indoor/outdoor bathrooms, satelliteTV, king beds, free broadband internet access. Shared facilities include a 14 m infinity pool, bale and jacuzzi.

voyage.name: Barong Resort and Spa
voyage.content: A/C rooms equipped with cableTV, mini-bar with lunch table, and coffee/tea maker.Outdoor swimming pool, jacuzzi, airport and city transfers, and currency exchange.

voyage.name: Como Shambhala Estate
voyage.content: This is one of Bali's most expensive places to stay, and more a collection of super homes than a mere hotel. 20 min north of Ubud, close to the village of Payangan.

voyage.name: Four Seasons Resort at Sayan
voyage.content: One of Bali's truly great hotels, over-looking the Sayan gorge. Suites in the main building, individual villas down by the river. Restaurant and in-house spa facilities. Free shuttle bus to Ubud town centre.

voyage.name: Komaneka at Bisma
voyage.content: Short distance from the town. Built on a steep hillside with an infinity edge pool and surrounded by terraced rice paddies with a river rushing below. Central hotel block has spacious, tastefully decorated suites, private villas, a wedding chapel and separate spa huts. Komaneka also has two other properties in Ubud, the central and slightly older Monkey Forest and the newer but rather remote Tanggayuda.

voyage.name: Maya Ubud
voyage.content: 10 hectares of land with fine villas, excellent spa and a good restaurant. Architecturally impressive resort with two free form swimming pools. Free shuttle to centre of Ubud.

voyage.name: Natura Villa Resort and Spa
voyage.content: Overlooking Petanu River.

voyage.name: Naya Ubud
voyage.content: Set within Balinese rice fields, three traditional structures (a Lumbumg, Gladak, and Joglo) house the 5 bedrooms in this boutique luxury resort, surrounded by tropical gardens and an infinity pool.

voyage.name: Pertiwi Resort and Spa
voyage.content: Combining traditional Balinese design with modern touches. Alang-alang (thatched) roof, bamboo ceiling, long glass windows. A/C, cableTV, mini-bar, coffee/tea maker. Swimming pools, free wifi access, and a spa.

voyage.name: Pita Maha Resort and Spa
voyage.content: Hill-side resort with 24 villas. Good restaurant, high quality spa and lovely pool with views.

voyage.name: The Purist Villas & Spa
voyage.address: Jl. Tirta Tawar, Banjar Kutuh Kaja
voyage.content: 14-villa boutique resort in the Ubud jungle, close to the Ubud Botanic Garden.

voyage.name: Santi Mandala Villa and Spa
voyage.content: Spa centre, poolside sunken bar and large private villas.

voyage.name: Ubud Hanging Gardens
voyage.content: On steep terraces overlooking the Ayung river and an ancient temple. 38 luxury villas, each with a heated private swimming pool. Villas with panoramic views of the valley, or riverside villas in the privacy of the gorge. Spa and innovative restaurant.

voyage.name: Viceroy Bali
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with four different grades of villa. Pristine valley setting, views from all the villas. In-house spa, good restaurant, shuttle buses into Ubud. A member of Small Leading Hotels of the World.

voyage.name: Waka Namya Resort and Spa
voyage.content: Resort in the "painters' village" of Penestanan, built in traditional Balinese style.

voyage.name: Wapa Di Ume Resort & Spa
voyage.content: Rural rice field setting 10 min north of Ubud town centre. Well maintained established resort. Good spa services and restaurant, and regular free shuttle buses into Ubud.

voyage.name: Villa Sabandari
voyage.content: A six room boutique hotel in the rice fields. Walking distance from the centre of Ubud.

voyage.name: Agung Khalia Villa
voyage.content: Private villas from studio to three bedroom and six bedroom. Panoramic rice field and Mount Agung views. Each villa has its own private pool, staff and full service. Only 10 min east from central Ubud in the same valley as the Maya Ubud resort, and close to Goa Gajah.

voyage.name: De Ubud Villas & Spa
voyage.content: 3 private pool villas located in central Ubud. Choice of 1 bedroom, 2 bedroom and 3 bedroom villas.

voyage.name: Kajane Mua Private Villa and Mansion
voyage.content: Private villas, each with its own private pool. Breakfast and afternoon tea is included in room price and can be brought to the villa each morning or taken at the Kajane Resto. Kajane Resto provides a large selection for each meal and drinks, and room service is available until 23:00 at no extra charge. A driver and clean van are provided for free transport around the Ubud area and at low cost to other areas of inter

voyage.name: Kayumanis Ubud Private Villa & Spa
voyage.content: 23 contemporary villas with private pool, fully-equipped gourmet kitchen and 24-hours butler service.

voyage.name: Villa di Abing
voyage.content: 3 storey, 3 bedroom, fully staffed villa, in central Ubud. Riverside pool, natural green views and within easy walking distance of Ubud town centre.

voyage.name: Jendela di Bali
voyage.content: This private villa in the hills near Ubud is like a 'village' of unique living spaces. A collection of handcrafted bales represent traditional Balinese and Indonesian Archipelago styles, creating a very authentic cultural experience. Facilities include a wet-edge infinity pool, media and meditation bale, lounge bale and two bedroom bales 'The White Elephant' and 'The Kingfisher'. The villa accommodates up to four and
